text:
alex: Heads-up — after last night's INT8 rollout to canary, we're seeing a p99 latency spike on the decoder path for long-context requests (~>512). Perfetto trace attached (see below).

maria: ugh. any obvious kernel hot spots?

alex: Perfetto flame shows a cluster of short host->device memcpy bursts during cold-starts, then long CPU-side dequant ops labeled `dequant_cpu` interleaved with `kv_prefetch`. NVTX: a bunch of kernels selected as `int8_conv_fallback_fp32` for certain layers.

sam: Can you paste the perfetto slice names? Also run `nsys` for a sample request, we need kernel timelines + host stacks.

alex: Paste of perfetto slices (snip):

```
flame:
  - memcpy_htod (0.2ms)
  - kv_prefetch (1.1ms)
  - dequant_cpu (3.6ms)
  - int8_qdot (0.5ms)
  - dequant_cpu (2.9ms)
  - kernel_wait (0.3ms)
```

alex: nsys command I ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt -o /tmp/run1 nsys_sample_runner --model canary --seq 1024 --batch 1`

infra-bot: Note: 2003334400 - canary deploy int8-quant-2026-03-17 succeeded.

jess: Maybe quantization path is triggering a host-side dequant for attention layer when KV cache size exceeds a page boundary. We saw similar in the FP8 experiment but not this bad.

sam: Agreed. Two hypotheses: 1) kernel selection logic chooses an INT8 kernel that requires an extra dequant on host for certain dim alignments; 2) batching heuristic caused KV cache churn so we keep refilling prefixes and hitting memcpy stalls.

maria: How reproducible? Is this only cold-start or sustained?

alex: Repro is higher on cold-start and when sequence length >=512. After steady-state, p99 drops but still 15% above baseline.

jess: Can we capture a short nsys with `--sample=cpu` to get host stack for the dequant calls? Also switch kernel logger to debug for the particular model shard.

sam: I'm running a quick instrumented run now. Command I pushed: `./tools/run_trace.sh --model canary --seq 1024 --trace nsys --sample-cpu --dump-kernel-log /tmp/klog`

alex: Kernel log excerpt (from /tmp/klog):

```
[2026-03-17T02:12:01Z] layer_35: selected kernel int8_matmul_vec
[2026-03-17T02:12:01Z] layer_35: fallback_to_fp32=true (alignment=7)
[2026-03-17T02:12:01Z] layer_35: dequant_op=host_dequant_async (cpu_ms=3.2)
[2026-03-17T02:12:01Z] kv_cache: page_boundary_cross=true, prefetch_batches=0
```

maria: that `alignment=7` stands out. Our int8 kernels require 8-byte alignment; odd-length heads cause fallback. We should either pad in kernel selection or add a lightweight GPU-side dequant kernel.

jess: Adding GPU dequant would cut host CPU latency but may increase kernel complexity. Do we have a microbench on `gpu_dequant_async`?

sam: I benchmarked a prototype yesterday: `gpu_dequant_async` ~0.6ms vs host_dequant 3.1ms for the same tile. Memory copy overhead still matters for KV prefetch though.

alex: Another angle — batching heuristics: when requests pile up, we form a big batch that crosses our KV page boundary heuristic and triggers extra prefetch rounds. That multiplies memcpy and host dequant. We should tweak the batcher to respect KV page boundaries more strictly (or split batches).

maria: Can we add a temporary metric: `dequant_host_ms_per_request` and `kv_memcpy_count` and alert when dequant_host_ms > 1ms?

alex: I'll add the metric to the telemetry PR and a canary rule. Also opening perf ticket: INF-3124 (repro + traces attached).

jess: For immediate mitigation, let's rollback the canary to last-known-good for that shard, or pin that model to fp8 where we've validated alignment. Which is cheaper?

sam: Rolling back canary for the shard reduces exposure quickly. Pinning to fp8 may increase token cost. I'd prefer rollback + quick fix.

alex: Rolling back now. infra-bot: `deploy rollback --target canary/shard-3`

infra-bot: Rollback triggered by alex at 2003334555. Deployment status: in-progress -> success at 2003334620.

maria: Good. After rollback, can we run a controlled ab test: 500 requests seq=1024, collect nsys+perfetto with warmup? Make sure to capture `nvtx` markers around `kv_prefetch` and `dequant`.

sam: Yep. I'll schedule the job on the perf pool and attach the traces to INF-3124.

alex: Long-term actions: (1) kernel selector to avoid host dequant fallbacks by preferring GPU-dequant implementation when alignment mismatch; (2) batcher change to avoid cross-page batching; (3) KV prefetch backoff during cold-start; (4) telemetry alerts. I'll draft RFC.

jess: Also add a unit test for odd-head counts ensuring we pick non-fallback kernel or pad layout.

maria: Thanks all. Leave notes in INF-3124 and ping if you need extra perf slots. :thumbsup:

sam: Adding perfetto permalink here once upload finishes: https://perfetto.dev/trace/?id=abc123def

alex: Uploads attached to ticket. Closing loop for now.
